note: vappa: flat wine, i.e. a worthless man (Piso).

english: Is anything of little profit open in the ledgers

english: as spent, as for me, who having followed my
note: expensum: entered on the debit side.

latin: praetorem refero datum lucello,
english: praetor record what was paid out as little profit?
note: A book-keeping joke: his only 'profit' is his outlay. The praetor is Memmius. The question mark is added for the sense of ecquidnam (6-8); Merrill prints a comma here and runs on into the quoted words of 9-10.

note: trabs: beam, i.e. penis; irrumare as in 16.1: he was exploited.

latin: farti estis. pete nobiles amicos.
english: you have been stuffed. Seek noble friends!

english: But on you many evils may the gods and goddesses
